Turn 2: fetch the history page for the series you will use. Turn 5: reply with the data note: Indiana series yes/no with evidence URL, exact series name and ID, first and last week dates, EIA release date on the page, retrieval date, anomalies. Never fill a gap with an estimate.

responsibilities: Check whether EIA publishes a weekly on-highway diesel series for Indiana and record the evidence (page URL and area list).
If not, pull Midwest (PADD 2), all types, weekly retail on-highway diesel and flag it as a stand-in.
Extract the 52 most recent weekly Monday prices up to the latest release with week date and price in $/gal.
Record series name, series ID, source URL, EIA release date and retrieval date.
Write the CSV and report the validation results.

created_roles.description: Transportation economist who follows ATRI's Operational Costs of Trucking benchmarking reports and knows how they define marginal cost per mile and the fuel line. Brings the industry benchmark the carrier's fuel cost is compared with.
created_roles.prompt: You are a trucking-economics researcher. Turn 1: web_search 'ATRI An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking' and any release newer than the 2024-data edition; identify the newest edition and release date. Turn 3: if fuel is not in the first source, fetch a second (ATRI PDF or reputable trade press) and note which is primary. Turn 4: compute fuel share = fuel per mile ÷ total per mile using only same-edition numbers (use python for the arithmetic) and note ATRI's diesel price and mpg basis if stated. Turn 5: output the benchmark table (metric, value, edition/data year, release date, URL, primary/secondary), a note on the newest-edition search, and a short caveats list. If the fuel component cannot be found, say exactly which figure is missing and give the best substitute with source and date, flagged as a substitute.

Record report title, data year, release date, URL and ATRI's stated diesel price or mpg basis as comparability caveats.
If the fuel figure is not readable, use the most reliable secondary source, label it, and give URL and date.

list

## Requirements:
R1: Get the weekly retail on-highway diesel price for Indiana for the most recent 52 weeks from EIA, and cite the series (name and series ID) and the week of each price.
R2: For each of the 52 weeks, compute the fuel surcharge per mile as ROUND((price − 1.25) ÷ 6.2, 2) and the fleet's total fuel cost for the week.
R3: Find the latest ATRI average marginal cost per mile for trucking and the share of it that is fuel (same report year).
R4: Compare the ATRI fuel cost per mile and fuel share with the carrier's average fuel cost per mile over the 52 weeks.
R5: Deliver an Excel workbook with weekly price, surcharge and fleet fuel cost, built with live formulas.
R6: Deliver a PNG line chart of weekly price and surcharge over the 52 weeks.
R7: Deliver a Word (docx) memo of at most 2 pages.
R8: The memo gives the surcharge for each 5-cent price band from $3.00 to $5.00, and the average, highest and lowest week.
R9: The memo gives the ATRI comparison and the source and date of every figure.

R1: Get the weekly retail on-highway diesel price for Indiana for the most recent 52 weeks from EIA, and cite the series (name and series ID) and the week of each price.

R3: Find the latest ATRI average marginal cost per mile for trucking and the share of it that is fuel (same report year).
R4: Compare the ATRI fuel cost per mile and share with the carrier's average fuel cost per mile over the 52 weeks.

## Givens and Assumptions:
- Fleet: 35 Class 8 tractors, 6.2 mpg, 2,300 miles per tractor per week (task).

- Fleet weekly miles = 35 × 2,300 = 80,500.
- Fleet weekly gallons = 80,500 ÷ 6.2 = 12,983.87 (about 12,984).
- Weekly fleet fuel cost = 12,983.87 × weekly price. Each $1.00 of price is about $12,984 per week.
- Annual (52-week) miles = 4,186,000. Annual gallons = 675,161.
- Carrier fuel cost per mile in a week = price ÷ 6.2. The 52-week average = average price ÷ 6.2, which equals total fuel cost ÷ total miles because weekly miles are constant.
- Surcharge at the band ends: (3.00 − 1.25) ÷ 6.2 = 0.2823, so $0.28. (5.00 − 1.25) ÷ 6.2 = 0.6048, so $0.60. A 5-cent price step is worth only $0.00806 per mile, so cent rounding makes the schedule step irregularly.

- Assumption: if EIA has no Indiana weekly series, use EIA Midwest (PADD 2) weekly all-types on-highway diesel, labelled as a stand-in [P1][P2].
- Assumption: each band's surcharge is computed at the band's floor price (price ≥ floor and < floor + $0.05), rounded to the cent. The last row is '$5.00 and above', with the formula given for higher prices.
- Assumption: fleet fuel cost uses constant gallons (12,983.87) × price, as the task specifies.

## Givens and Assumptions:
- Fleet: 35 Class 8 tractors (heavy-duty trucks over 33,000 lb GVWR, i.e. semi tractors), 6.2 mpg, 2,300 miles per tractor per week (task).
- Surcharge formula: ROUND((weekly price − $1.25) ÷ 6.2, 2) per mile (task).
- Fleet weekly miles = 35 × 2,300 = 80,500.
- Fleet weekly gallons = 80,500 ÷ 6.2 = 12,983.87 (about 12,984).
- Weekly fleet fuel cost = 12,983.87 × weekly price. Each $1.00 of price is about $12,984 per week.
- 52-week miles = 80,500 × 52 = 4,186,000. 52-week gallons = 12,983.87 × 52 = 675,161.
- Carrier fuel cost per mile in a week = price ÷ 6.2. The 52-week average = average price ÷ 6.2, which equals total fuel cost ÷ total miles because weekly miles are constant.
- Surcharge at the band ends: (3.00 − 1.25) ÷ 6.2 = 0.2823, so $0.28. (5.00 − 1.25) ÷ 6.2 = 0.6048, so $0.60. A 5-cent price step is worth only $0.00806 per mile, so cent rounding makes the schedule step irregularly.

## Requirements:
R1: Get the weekly retail on-highway diesel price for Indiana for the most recent 52 weeks from EIA, and cite the series (name and series ID) and the week of each price.
R2: For each of the 52 weeks, compute the fuel surcharge per mile as ROUND((price − 1.25) ÷ 6.2, 2) and the fleet's total fuel cost for the week.
R3: Find the latest ATRI average marginal cost per mile for trucking and the share of it that is fuel (same report year).
R4: Compare the ATRI fuel cost per mile and fuel share with the carrier's average fuel cost per mile over the 52 weeks.
R5: Deliver an Excel workbook with weekly price, surcharge and fleet fuel cost, built with live formulas.
R6: Deliver a PNG line chart of weekly price and surcharge over the 52 weeks.
R7: Deliver a Word (docx) memo of at most 2 pages.
R8: The memo gives the surcharge for each 5-cent price band from $3.00 to $5.00, and the average, highest and lowest week.
R9: The memo gives the ATRI comparison and the source and date of every figure.
R10: State any figure that could not be obtained and what was used instead (e.g. no Indiana series, so Midwest PADD 2 used).
R11: The final answer opens, word for word, with the line: I read "weekly retail on-highway diesel price for Indiana" as EIA weekly retail on-highway diesel prices, all types, for the state of Indiana (if EIA publishes a state series); if you meant EIA Midwest (PADD 2) regional weekly diesel price used as a stand-in for Indiana or EIA U.S. national average weekly diesel price, the answer below may not apply.
R12: Plan and model the carrier as it runs: 35 Class 8 tractors (heavy-duty semi tractors over 33,000 lb GVWR) that average 6.2 mpg and about 2,300 miles per week each, with these figures held as workbook inputs and used for the fleet fuel cost and per-mile figures.

## Givens and Assumptions:
- Fleet: 35 Class 8 tractors (heavy-duty trucks over 33,000 lb GVWR, i.e. semi tractors), 6.2 mpg, 2,300 miles per tractor per week (task).
- Surcharge formula: ROUND((weekly price − $1.25) ÷ 6.2, 2) per mile (task).
- Fleet weekly miles = 35 × 2,300 = 80,500.
- Fleet weekly gallons = 80,500 ÷ 6.2 = 12,983.87 (about 12,984).
- Weekly fleet fuel cost = 12,983.87 × weekly price. Each $1.00 of price is about $12,984 per week.
- 52-week miles = 80,500 × 52 = 4,186,000. 52-week gallons = 12,983.87 × 52 = 675,161.
- Carrier fuel cost per mile in a week = price ÷ 6.2. The 52-week average = average price ÷ 6.2, which equals total fuel cost ÷ total miles because weekly miles are constant.
- Surcharge at the band ends: (3.00 − 1.25) ÷ 6.2 = 0.2823, so $0.28. (5.00 − 1.25) ÷ 6.2 = 0.6048, so $0.60. A 5-cent price step is worth only $0.00806 per mile, so cent rounding makes the schedule step irregularly.
- The 5-cent bands from $3.00 to $5.00 inclusive give 41 band floors (3.00, 3.05, …, 5.00).
- Context from planning search: EIA PADD 2 weekly prices are published and were about $6.26-6.29 in the latest look versus about $3.67 a year earlier [P1][P3]. Many weeks may therefore fall above $5.00, outside the requested band range.
- Context from planning search: ATRI reported $2.27 per mile for 2023 and $2.260 for 2024 [P4][P5]. A newer edition may exist and the team must verify it.
- Assumption: if EIA has no Indiana weekly series, use EIA Midwest (PADD 2) weekly all-types on-highway diesel, labelled as a stand-in [P1][P2].
- Assumption: each band's surcharge is computed at the band's floor price (price ≥ floor and < floor + $0.05), rounded to the cent. The last row is '$5.00 and above', with the formula given for higher prices.
- Assumption: fleet fuel cost uses constant gallons (12,983.87) × price, as the task specifies.

## Open Questions:
- question: Does EIA publish a weekly Indiana on-highway diesel series? | assumption: Probably not; EIA's weekly diesel series cover the US, PADDs and a few states and cities [P1][P2]. Step 1 confirms this on the EIA page. If there is none, use Midwest (PADD 2) and say so in every deliverable. If one exists, use it.
- question: Which price within each 5-cent band is the surcharge computed at? | assumption: The band floor, stated in the memo. The workbook band table is driven by formulas from the floor price column.
- question: What should the memo say about weeks or current prices above $5.00 or below $3.00? | assumption: Give the count of weeks outside the $3.00-$5.00 table and the formula; put a few reference rows above $5 in the workbook only. The memo table stays at $3.00-$5.00.
- question: Which ATRI report counts as 'latest'? | assumption: The most recent 'Operational Costs of Trucking' edition, with total marginal cost per mile and fuel cost per mile taken from the same edition and its data year stated.

plan.do: 1) Search for the newest ATRI Operational Costs of Trucking edition and confirm no newer release exists. 2) Extract total marginal cost per mile and fuel cost per mile from that same edition with data year and release date. 3) Compute fuel share = fuel ÷ total. 4) Note ATRI's diesel price and mpg basis and other comparability caveats. 5) If fuel is only in a secondary source, label it; if a figure is missing, name it and give the substitute.
plan.output: table: metric | value | edition/data year | release date | URL | primary or secondary, plus list: comparability caveats
plan.done_when: The table gives total cost per mile, fuel cost per mile and fuel share from one edition; each figure has a URL and a date; the newest-edition check is documented; any missing figure and its substitute are named.

plan.text: [Fleet Cost Modeler & Deliverables Engineer]: Build the Excel workbook with live formulas
plan.title: Build the Excel workbook with live formulas
plan.do: 1) Build Inputs (35 trucks, 2,300 miles, 6.2 mpg, $1.25 base) and Weekly with live formulas for surcharge, gallons, fleet cost and cost per mile. 2) Build Bands (41 floors, $3.00-$5.00, formula surcharge, plus reference rows above $5). 3) Build Summary (average/high/low with week dates, 52-week totals, count of weeks outside $3-$5, ATRI comparison). 4) Build Sources with the stand-in flag. 5) Recompute every row with Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP and assert it matches; recalculate in LibreOffice if available. 6) Report key numbers.
plan.output: list: file name diesel_fuel_surcharge.xlsx, sheet inventory, key figures (average, high and low week, surcharge range, 52-week fleet fuel cost, average fuel cost per mile, ATRI comparison), recomputation result
plan.done_when: Weekly has 52 data rows with live formulas referencing Inputs; Bands has 41 floor rows; Summary and Sources sheets exist with the stand-in flag; the Decimal recomputation matches for all 52 weeks; key figures are reported.

plan.text: [Fleet Cost Modeler & Deliverables Engineer]: Draw the PNG line chart of price and surcharge
plan.title: Draw the PNG line chart of price and surcharge
plan.do: 1) Read eia_weekly.csv and compute the surcharge per week with Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP of (price − 1.25) ÷ 6.2 to match the workbook. 2) Draw a dual-axis line chart (price left in $/gal, surcharge right in $/mile) with a title naming the series and 52-week date range, labelled axes and a source note, noting the stand-in if PADD 2. 3) Save at ≥1200 px wide and report the size.
plan.output: list: file name diesel_price_surcharge.png, pixel size, series and date range shown
plan.done_when: diesel_price_surcharge.png exists; it is at least 1200 px wide; it shows both lines for 52 weeks; it has labelled axes, a title with series and date range, and a source note.

plan.text: [Numbers & Sources Verifier]: Verify data, workbook and chart
plan.title: Verify data, workbook and chart
plan.do: 1) Recompute all 52 surcharges and fleet costs independently from the raw CSV and compare with the workbook; confirm the 35 / 2,300 / 6.2 inputs. 2) Check formulas are live and reference Inputs, dates are consecutive Mondays, and average/high/low/bands are right. 3) Re-fetch at least 3 EIA prices (first, last, random) and the ATRI total and fuel figures at source. 4) Check the PNG matches the data and the stand-in is flagged. 5) Issue a PASS/FAIL verdict with defects and fixes.
plan.output: memo: Verdict (PASS/FAIL), table of checks run with results, defects and required fixes
plan.done_when: A PASS/FAIL verdict is given; the 52-week reconciliation result is listed; at least 3 EIA re-checks and the ATRI re-check are listed; each defect has a fix instruction. A FAIL sends defects back to step 1, 3 or 4 before step 6 runs.

plan.text: [Fleet Cost Modeler & Deliverables Engineer]: Write the ≤2-page Word memo
plan.title: Write the ≤2-page Word memo
plan.do: 1) Fix any step 5 defects first. 2) Write the memo from verified numbers only: Basis and interpretation (state if PADD 2 stands in for Indiana), Surcharge schedule (41 bands in 3 column blocks, band-floor convention, formula for prices above $5, count of weeks outside $3-$5), 52-week summary (average, highest, lowest week with dates), ATRI comparison with caveats, Sources and dates table, Figures not obtained and substitutes. 3) Convert to PDF to count pages, or estimate and flag if no converter, and trim to ≤2 pages.
plan.output: memo: fuel_surcharge_memo.docx with headings Basis, Surcharge schedule, 52-week summary, ATRI comparison, Sources and dates, Figures not obtained
plan.done_when: The docx exists and is ≤2 pages; a table holds all 41 band rows; average, highest and lowest week are given with dates; the ATRI comparison is given; every figure has a source and date; stand-in and not-obtained figures are stated.

plan.title: Verify the memo against the workbook and sources

givens: Fleet: 35 Class 8 tractors (heavy-duty trucks over 33,000 lb GVWR, i.e. semi tractors), 6.2 mpg, 2,300 miles per tractor per week (task).
Surcharge formula: ROUND((weekly price − $1.25) ÷ 6.2, 2) per mile (task).
Weekly fleet fuel cost = 12,983.87 × weekly price. Each $1.00 of price is about $12,984 per week.
Carrier fuel cost per mile in a week = price ÷ 6.2. The 52-week average = average price ÷ 6.2, which equals total fuel cost ÷ total miles because weekly miles are constant.

Surcharge at the band ends: (3.00 − 1.25) ÷ 6.2 = 0.2823, so $0.28. (5.00 − 1.25) ÷ 6.2 = 0.6048, so $0.60. A 5-cent price step is worth only $0.00806 per mile, so cent rounding makes the schedule step irregularly.
The 5-cent bands from $3.00 to $5.00 inclusive give 41 band floors (3.00, 3.05, …, 5.00).

Context from planning search: EIA PADD 2 weekly prices are published and were about $6.26-6.29 in the latest look versus about $3.67 a year earlier [P1][P3]. Many weeks may therefore fall above $5.00, outside the requested band range.
Context from planning search: ATRI reported $2.27 per mile for 2023 and $2.260 for 2024 [P4][P5]. A newer edition may exist and the team must verify it.
Assumption: if EIA has no Indiana weekly series, use EIA Midwest (PADD 2) weekly all-types on-highway diesel, labelled as a stand-in [P1][P2].

Assumption: each band's surcharge is computed at the band's floor price (price ≥ floor and < floor + $0.05), rounded to the cent. The last row is '$5.00 and above', with the formula given for higher prices.
Assumption: fleet fuel cost uses constant gallons (12,983.87) × price, as the task specifies.
risks: EIA has no Indiana weekly series (likely) [P1][P2]. Decision in step 1: use Midwest (PADD 2) and label it a stand-in in all three files and the final answer; if an Indiana series exists, use it and drop the stand-in wording.

Recent prices may be well above $5.00 [P1][P3], so many weeks may fall outside the $3.00-$5.00 band schedule. Step 3 counts these weeks, the memo gives the count and the formula, and the workbook has reference rows.

The latest ATRI edition may be newer than the 2024 data [P4][P5], or the fuel line may be hard to read from a gated PDF. Step 2 checks for newer releases; secondary-only figures are labelled and dated.
ATRI's fuel figure rests on its own diesel price and mpg and is not strictly comparable with this carrier's price ÷ 6.2; the memo states this caveat.
EIA history pages may be hard to parse within 5 turns. Step 1 is limited to one series and validates the CSV in the same step.
Excel ROUND and Python rounding can differ on exact halves; verification uses Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP and lists any cent mismatches.
The 41-row band table plus other content may overflow 2 pages. Use a 3-block table at 8-9 pt and check the page count via PDF conversion; if no converter exists, flag the count as an estimate.
